desc:
Given a rectangular grid of integers matrix and an integer target, count the non-empty submatrices whose elements add up to target. A submatrix is a block of consecutive rows and consecutive columns; two submatrices are different if their top-left or bottom-right corners differ.

matrix = [[1, -1],
          [-1, 1]], target = 0
matching: the two rows, the two columns and the whole 2x2 grid
result = 5
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: Fix the top and bottom rows of the submatrix. What remains is choosing a range of columns.
For a fixed pair of rows, sum each column between them to get a 1D array. A submatrix is then a contiguous subarray of this array.

Counting 1D subarrays with sum exactly target is done with prefix sums and a hash map of how often each prefix sum occurred. Repeat for all O(R2) row pairs, extending the column sums as the bottom row moves down.
editorial: Fix the top row t and sweep the bottom row b from t downwards, maintaining col[c] = the sum of column c over rows t..b; adding one row is O(C). Every submatrix with these two row bounds corresponds to a contiguous range of columns, whose sum is a subarray sum of col.

Count subarrays of col with sum target using a dictionary of prefix sums (starting with {0: 1}): for each column prefix P, add seen[P - target] and then record P. This gives O(R2 C) time and O(C) space, versus O(R2 C2) for a straightforward 2D prefix-sum enumeration. Make rows the smaller dimension in an implementation if you want the best constant factor.
